rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers recite ليهب with yāʾ, meaning God gives Mary the boy.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ونافع ويعقوب: (ليهب) بالياء بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first parse treats لأهب as a quotation of God's words: 'Your Lord said, I will give you.'
rows.anchor: بتقدير: قال ربك، لأهب لك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Gabriel says 'I will give' by God's command; the glad tidings make it as if he had given her the child.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: لأهب بأمر الله غلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse attributes the child to Gabriel as immediate cause: he breathed into Mary, while God created the child from the breath.
rows.anchor: نفخ جبريل فيها، والله تعالى خلق الولد من تلك النفخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can create bodies, so creation cannot literally be attributed to Gabriel; the first explanation is best.
rows.anchor: لأن خلق الأجسام ليس بمقدور لأحد سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means throwing or casting; the author connects it to the Qur'anic expression, wine made by soaking, foundlings, and the prohibited sale custom of munābadha.
rows.anchor: النبذ: هو الطرح والإلقاء، والانتباذ افتعال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdha means a nearby side, close enough that a tossed object would reach; eastern means the direction of sunrise.
rows.anchor: ونبذة بفتح النون وضمها أي: ناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy may mean sexual wrongdoing, oppression, or envy; its root is seeking, as in 'not seeking' and seeking something for another.
rows.anchor: وأصل الباب: الطلب، والبغاء بضم الباء: الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's question expresses wonder at the violation of ordinary custom, not doubt about God's power; another view makes it wonder at God's favor.
rows.anchor: ولكن لما نقض به العادة، وقيل: بل تعجب لنعمة الله عليها

rows.speaker: الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce نسيا with an open nūn; the others use kasra. Both are dialect variants, like الوتر and الوتر, and mean something forgotten.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم: نسيا بفتح النون

rows.speaker: الحسن وشيبة ونافع ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers use kasra in من تحتها; the others use fatḥa. Either reading allows Gabriel or Jesus as the caller.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وشيبة ونافع ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: On the kasra reading, Gabriel calls Mary from below the mountain.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو جبريل ناداها من سفل الجبل

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view says Jesus called from beneath Mary as he emerged.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عيسى لما خرج من بطن أمه من تحتها

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وحماد عن عاصم ونصير عن الكسائي
rows.claim: One reading has يساقط with yāʾ and doubled sīn, referring to the masculine palm trunk.
rows.anchor: قراءة البراء بن عازب ويعقوب وأبي حاتم وحماد عن عاصم

rows.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Another reading uses feminine tāʾ, fatḥa on tāʾ and qāf, and a light sīn.
rows.anchor: قراءة الأعمش وحمزة وأبو عبيدة بالتاء وفتحها وفتح القاف

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads تساقط with ḍamma on tāʾ, light sīn, and kasra on qāf.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم بضم التاء وتخفيف السين وكسر القاف

rows.speaker: باقي القراء
rows.claim: The remaining readers double sīn by assimilation of the original two tāʾs; lightening drops one tāʾ, and feminine tāʾ refers to the palm.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: قراءة الباقين بفتح التاء والقاف وتشديد السين على الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayyin means easy, accomplished without burden or difficulty; its opposite is difficult.
rows.anchor: الهين: السهل، وهو التأتي من غير كلفة ومشقة

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Arabs praise the lightened pair هين لين and censure the doubled form.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: العرب تمدح بالهين واللين مخففة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another grammarian treats the forms as one expression whose original doubled form is lightened; a poem illustrates the lightened form.
rows.anchor: قال غيره: هما شيء واحد والأصل التثقيل يخفف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqḍiyy means a matter firmly decreed to occur; the word derives from decisive judgment.
rows.anchor: والمقضي: المفضول من الأمور أي: المحكوم حتما أنه يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence.
rows.anchor: والفاء للتعقيب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mary conceived, the child was formed, and she gave birth within one hour at midday; she was ten and had menstruated twice.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل: حملت به في ساعة، وصور في ساعة، ووضعته في ساعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Labor forced Mary to the palm trunk; مخاض means labor pains.
rows.anchor: فأجاءها المخاض أي: ألجأها، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One account describes a dry desert palm without fronds; another says it was winter and the tree had no crown, making the fruit a sign.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان جذع نخلة يابسة في الصحراء ولم يكن لها سعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in the palm phrase refers to a particular familiar palm, not palms in general.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام دخلا للعهد لا للجنس

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: God made a trunk grow, and Mary clung to it as a woman clings to another during labor; another account places the birth near Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أنبت الله جذعا فتعلقت به كما تتعلق المرأة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Nasiy means something abandoned or left behind.
rows.anchor: كنت نسيا منسيا متروكا، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Nasiy is something forgotten and no longer mentioned or known.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نسيا لا يذكر ولا يعرف، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Nasiy may mean discarded menstrual blood or cloth.
rows.anchor: قيل: حيضة ملقاة، عن عكرمة، والضحاك، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Nasiy may mean a miscarried fetus.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو السقط، عن الربيع

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Nasiy may mean something dead or destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كالشيء الهالك، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Nasiy may mean that Mary had never been created.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني: لم أخلق، عن عطاء

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Other views take it as a trivial forgotten thing or what a woman expels for fear of becoming ill.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو ما نسي من شيء حقير

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Mary wished for death to avoid disgrace and people's accusations, or because of the severity of labor, or fear that people would sin because of her and humiliate her.
rows.anchor: قيل: لخوف الفضيحة وطعن الناس

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: One specific view attributes Mary's wish for death to the severe labor pains.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما أصابها من شدة الطلق، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wishing for death is not blameworthy when done with insight, as Mary did and as is related of ʿAlī; other views say vexation or embarrassment prompted her.
rows.anchor: وأما تمني الموت فلا يكره إذا كان عن بصيرة كما تمنت هي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Mary wished she had not become widely known and discussed despite her reputation for piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قالت استحياء من الناس، عن السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Gabriel called to Mary from beneath her.
rows.anchor: قيل: ناداها جبريل، عن ابن عباس، والسدي، والضحاك، وقتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد ووهب وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد وأبو علي والأصم
rows.claim: Jesus called to Mary from beneath her.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عيسى، عن مجاهد، ووهب، وسعيد بن جبير، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sariy means a river; other views call it a small channel or stream.
rows.anchor: قيل: نهرا، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب والأصم
rows.claim: Sariy may mean a small channel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جدولا، عن البراء بن عازب، والأصم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Sariy means a small river for Mary to drink from and wash after childbirth.
rows.anchor: قيل: النهر الصغير، عن إبراهيم، والضحاك، وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد وأبو علي
rows.claim: Sariy may mean Jesus, a noble and distinguished servant; al-Ḥasan swears he was such a servant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السري عيسى، عن الحسن، وابن زيد، وأبي علي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Under you may mean the river runs beneath Mary's command, as in the verse about rivers running beneath; it may instead mean physically below her.
rows.anchor: قيل: جعل النهر يجري تحت أمرها وتمسكه بأمرها

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Gabriel struck the ground with his foot and a sweet spring appeared; another view credits Jesus' foot.
rows.anchor: قيل: ضرب جبريل برجله فظهر ماء عذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadhʿ may mean the whole palm or its branch; تساقط means it drops fruit onto Mary, and الرطب الجني is tender, freshly picked dates.
rows.anchor: يقال: الجذع النخلة نفسها، وقيل: الجذع الغصن أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet chewed dates and performed tahnik for the Companions' newborns.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يمضغ التمر ويحنك به أولاد الصحابة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha calls chewing a date and rubbing it into a newborn's mouth Sunnah.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة: أن من السنة أن يمضغ التمر ويدلك به فم المولود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression قرّت عينا has dialectal forms and associates settled joy with coolness and stillness; one view says 'may God rest your eyes' means make you sleep.
rows.anchor: فلذلك يقال: أقر الله عينك: أعطاه حتى تقر عينه

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Qarūr is cold water used for washing, illustrating the root's association with coolness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت القرور الماء البارد يغسل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhr is a vow establishing an obligation.
rows.anchor: والنذر: عقد إيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fary literally refers to cutting for repair, later extended to astonishing deeds or falsehood.
rows.anchor: الفري: القطع للإصلاح، فريت الشيء أفريه فريا

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Fari may mean being bewildered, while afraytuhu means I ruined it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت فري إذا تحير، وأفريته إذا أفسدته

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Fary means something astonishing, while firya means a lie.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الفرى: العجب، والفرية: الكذب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The term derives from trimming leather properly and is extended metaphorically to falsehood, which is invalid or wrongly cut.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الفري مأخوذ من فري الأديم قطعته قطع إصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahd is a bed or cradle prepared for an infant.
rows.anchor: والمهد: ما وطي للصبي من السرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In من كان في المهد, kāna is an added emphatic word, illustrated by poetry and 3:110.
rows.anchor: (كان) في قوله: كان في المهد زائدة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce قول الحق with fatḥa on the lām; the others use nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب: قول الحق بنصب اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One nominative parse makes قول الحق a predicate describing Jesus.
rows.anchor: ذاك الذي قدمنا من صفته قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse attaches it to Jesus, so he and his word are truth.
rows.anchor: أن يكون تابعا لعيسى كأنه قيل: ذلك عيسى وكلمته كلمة الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baraka is growth of good; tabarruk seeks blessing and derives from firmness.
rows.anchor: البركة: نماء الخير. والتبرك: طلب البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer means supplication linguistically and a defined worship with acts and pillars in religious law.
rows.anchor: وفي الشرع: عبادة مخصوصة تشتمل على أفعال وأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وبرّا is coordinated with 'made me a prophet'; مباركا can be understood as 'made me dutiful to my mother.'
rows.anchor: (وبرا) عطف على قوله: (وجعلني نبيا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mubārak means one who teaches goodness.
rows.anchor: قيل: معلما للخير، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Mubārak can mean beneficial or a blessing to followers of Jesus' religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نفاعا، وقيل: مباركا على من تبع ديني

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Mubārak may mean steadfast in God's religion and obedience.
rows.anchor: ثابتا على دين الله تعالى وطاعته، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was commanded to establish prayer and pay alms; zakāt may also mean purification from sins.
rows.anchor: أوصاني أمرني بالصلاة والزكاة يعني: إقامة الصلاة وأداء الزكاة

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: A view al-Aṣamm transmits says Meccan occurrences of zakāt mean goodness in general, while Medinan ones mean wealth.
rows.anchor: أن كل ما ذكر من الزكاة في المكي فهو الخير كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command lasts as long as Jesus remains alive and morally accountable.
rows.anchor: ما بقيت حيا مكلفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' filial piety is attributed to God because God commanded, guided, enabled, and aided him; religious manners credit God with virtues He supports.
rows.anchor: وأضافه إليه تعالى؛ لأنه بأمره ولطفه صار كذلك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Not being tyrannical and wretched may mean God did not assign Jesus their punishment, curse, and blame.
rows.anchor: لم ينزلني منزلة الجبارين الأشقياء في العقاب واللعن والذم، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section says religious argument is sound.
rows.anchor: وتدل على صحة الحجاج في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage commends humility and condemns arrogance.
rows.anchor: وتدل على حسن التواضع وقبح التكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage establishes a mother's right.
rows.anchor: وتدل على حق الوالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fabricated claims about Jesus; the truth is what the Qur'an states and Muslims affirm.
rows.anchor: أن الحق ما نطق به الكتاب وما عليه المسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above deficiencies, including bodily and accidental properties, and is free of injustice and evil acts.
rows.anchor: منزه عن صفات النقص، وهو كل صفة تخص الأجسام والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot take a child, since offspring implies shared kind, unlike friendship.
rows.anchor: لأنه يقتضى الجنس خلاف الخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be spoken by Jesus.
rows.anchor: يحتمل ثلاثة أوجه: أن يكون كلام عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may begin God's speech or be a divine instruction to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو كلام الله تعالى ابتداء، أو أمر النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone creates, He alone must be worshipped.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا كان هو الخالق وحده فوجب أن يعبد وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a clear, manifest way.
rows.anchor: هذا صراط مستقيم أي: طريق واضح بين

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Other explanations call the straight path the way to monotheism, Paradise, or upright religion.
rows.anchor: قيل: طريق إلى التوحيد، مستقيم قيل: إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The factions may be Christians divided into Jacobites, Nestorians, and Melkites over Jesus.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم النصارى افترقوا في عيسى فرقا ثلاثا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وأبو علي
rows.claim: The factions may be Jews and Christians among the People of the Book, who disagreed about Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اليهود والنصارى من أهل الكتاب اختلفوا في عيسى، عن قتادة، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: The factions may be all unbelievers united against the Messenger despite their own disagreements.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم جميع الكفار تحزبوا على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions are groups of people who gathered and split into parties.
rows.anchor: فاختلف الأحزاب الجماعة منهم من بينهم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Wayl is an expression of threat or means punishment; the Day's assembly can be a public spectacle.
rows.anchor: قيل: الويل كلمة وعيد، وقيل: العذاب من مشهد يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is called great because of its terrors.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة، سمي عظيما لعظم أهواله

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: At Judgment they hear and see what breaks their hearts and destroys them, though it will not help them.
rows.anchor: ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم به يوم القيامة، ولكن لا ينفعهم، عن الحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The warning makes them hear and see the description of their fate as if witnessing it.
rows.anchor: أسمعهم ما أنزلنا عليك من وعيدهم، وأبصرهم بالوصف لهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: They will hear and see on the day they come to God, but now they are heedless and do not believe.
rows.anchor: هم بصراء سامعون يوم يأتوننا لكنهم اليوم في ضلال وغفلة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the tāʾ in يا أبت throughout the Qur'an; the others use kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر [(ياأبت)] بفتح التاء في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ intensifies the possessive address; kasra seeks the possessive yāʾ and the stop retains tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإنما دخلت التاء في يا أبت للمبالغة في تحقيق الإضافة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj permits stopping with hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج الوقف بالهاء

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another analysis makes tāʾ replace the possessive yāʾ; fatḥa can represent يا أبتاه.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التاء عوض من ياء الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq derives from truthfulness and describes someone habitually truthful.
rows.anchor: الصديق: فعيل من الصدق، وهو الذي يكون عادته الصدق

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq may mean frequent affirmation of truth or habitual truthfulness.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مسلم. وقيل: هو كثير التصديق بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṣī and ʿāṣī mean the same thing, like ʿalīm and ʿālim.
rows.anchor: والعصي والعاصي بمعنى، كالعليم والعالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinating wāw shifts from the story of Zechariah to Abraham's story.
rows.anchor: واو عطف جملة على جملة كأنه قيل: في الكتاب قصة زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna begins a new sentence; kāna may describe an ongoing state, mean 'became,' or span Abraham's whole life.
rows.anchor: وكسر إنه للاستئناف كان صديقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takūna is coordinated with yamsaska: Abraham fears punishment touching his father and his father becoming Satan's ally.
rows.anchor: تكون نصب معطوف على قوله: أن يمسك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq means abundant affirmation of religious truths.
rows.anchor: كثير التصديق في أمور الدين، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq means always truthful about reports from God.
rows.anchor: كثير الصدق فيما يخبر عن الله حتى لا يكذب، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is a religious title for someone of exalted rank.
rows.anchor: الصديق من أسماء الدين يسمى به من عظمت رتبته، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham addresses his father Āzar, who was an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: لأبيه آزر وكان كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship may mean worship, supplication, submission, or obedience; the objects may be idols or all celestial bodies and other things his people worshipped.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد الأصنام، عن أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a benefactor possessing original blessings—God, powerful, knowing, living, eternal—deserves worship; idols lack these attributes.
rows.anchor: العبادة يستحقها المنعم بأصول النعم وهو الإله القادر العالم الحي القديم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The knowledge Abraham received may be religious knowledge, knowledge of resurrection, or knowledge of God's promise, threat, and punishment for worshipping another.
rows.anchor: قيل: علمت من علوم الدين ما لم تعلم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Knowledge may mean its means: evidence, revelation, and prophethood.
rows.anchor: من أسباب العلم، من الأدلة والوحي والنبوة ما لم يأتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirāṭan sawiyyan is an upright path of truth; other views call it the road to Paradise or escape from Hell.
rows.anchor: طريقا مستويا في الدين وهو طريق الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not worshipping Satan means refusing his commands; obedience is figuratively worship. The author prefers this over taking Satan as leaders or idol worship prompted by Satan.
rows.anchor: لا تطعه فيما يدعوك إليه فتكون بمنزلة من عبده

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Satan may stand for the people's leaders.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد بالشيطان رؤساؤهم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Because Satan prompted idol worship, the people can be described as worshipping Satan.
rows.anchor: عبدوا الأصنام بدعاء الشيطان فكأنهم عبدوا الشيطان

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The phrase 'I fear' may mean fear, or 'I know,' said out of concern for Abraham.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو من الخوف، وقيل: معناه أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If fear is literal, both persistence in unbelief and repentance remain possible while the father is accountable; if it means knowledge, Abraham knew he persisted.
rows.anchor: فما دام مكلفا فكلا الأمرين فيه جائز

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Satan's ally may be his companion in Hell, one who joins his curse and abandonment, or one whose affairs are left to Satan.
rows.anchor: قيل: قرينا في النار، وقيل: وليا، أي: لاحقا بالشيطان

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Walī may mean one who follows and joins Satan in curse and abandonment.
rows.anchor: واللاحق يسمى التالي، والذي يتلو الشيء والذي يليه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Walī may mean Satan is put in charge of the father's affairs.
rows.anchor: يكون أمرك موكولا إلى الشيطان حتى يلي أمرك، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying 'you become Satan's ally' is more shaming than saying 'Satan is your ally'; it warns that Satan alone cannot truly aid him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال: (تكون للشيطان وليا) ولم يقل وليك الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage refutes the view of the أصحاب المعارف because Abraham says he received knowledge his father lacked.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قول أصحاب المعارف؛ لأنه نص أنه جاءه من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge must invite others and clarify religion.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن من خص بالعلم يجب عليه الدعاء وبيان الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allegiance to disobedient humans and jinn must be severed; Hell's people have no real helper if Satan is their ally.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب قطع موالاة العصاة من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father was an unbeliever, as other Qur'anic verses say, so the plain meaning should not be displaced by figurative reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن أبا إبراهيم كان كافرا، وقد ذكر في آي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and following are acts of human agents, contradicting the opponents' doctrine about created acts.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة والاتباع فعل العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghba in something is desire to obtain it for benefit; raghba away from it is turning aside from harm. It can also mean abundant giving.
rows.anchor: الرغبة في الشيء نقيض الرغبة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intihāʾ means refraining from a forbidden act; its root concerns reaching a limit.
rows.anchor: والانتهاء: الامتناع من الفعل المنهي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajm means stoning or insult; its root is stones.
rows.anchor: الرجم: الرمي بالحجارة، والرجم: الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maly means a span of time; the dual may denote night and day, and respite prolongs someone's days.
rows.anchor: مليا: حينا ومدة، يقال: أقام ملاوة من دهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafiyy means assiduous, thorough, and exhaustive; related forms describe lavish honoring or intense questioning.
rows.anchor: والحفي: المستقصي في السؤال، وأصل الباب: الاستقصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham chooses religion over helping his father and emigration over homeland; he withdraws from them and their worship.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أنه يختار الدين على مساعدة الأب، والهجرة على الوطن

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: What they call upon means idols; alternatively, calling means worship.
rows.anchor: قيل: تدعونه إلها وهي الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ʿasā expresses certainty: Abraham will not be wretched in praying to his Lord as his people were in praying to idols; he speaks humbly.
rows.anchor: عسى هو هنا واجب ومعناه: لا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Abraham separated from his people by migrating to the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: قيل: فارقهم إلى الأرض المقدسة، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Abraham Isaac and grandson Jacob and made all three prophets to be followed in religion.
rows.anchor: وهبنا له أعطينا له إسحاق ويعقوب ابنا وابن ابن

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: God's mercy may mean wealth and children, prophethood and scripture, or religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: قيل: المال والولد، وقيل: النبوة والكتاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A high truthful mention means good praise; all religious communities praise and show loyalty to Abraham's family.
rows.anchor: قيل: ثناء حسنا، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: A truthful tongue may mean revelation and God's command that they convey it to His servants.
rows.anchor: اللسان الصدق وما آتاهم من وحيه

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: It may mean their honorable and praiseworthy reputation or the blessing on Abraham in the prayer testimony.
rows.anchor: رجل صدق أي: محمود

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: It may mean their mention in scripture: truthful divine books speak of them like a tongue.
rows.anchor: اللسان الصدق: ذكرهم في الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's expression لسان means praise or report.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Threats instead of answering Abraham's argument illustrate the helplessness of falsehood that abandons proof.
rows.anchor: على عجزه عن جواب الحجة، وهكذا طريقة كل مبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'when he withdrew' supports using iʿtizāl for withdrawal from evil.
rows.anchor: اسم الاعتزال لا يرد إلا في الاعتزال عن الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever is permitted either rationally or on condition he later believes.
rows.anchor: على جواز الاستغفار للكافر إما عقلا أو بشرط الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abraham emigrated, God raised his rank; this is God's custom with His servants.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه لما هاجر رفعه الله

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the lām of مخلصا; the rest use kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: (مخلصا) بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, it means Moses devoted worship to God; Muqātil also says he was a monotheist Muslim.
rows.anchor: قيل: أخلص العبادة لله، وقيل: كان موحدا مسلما، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, it means God chose Moses for prophethood and its gifts.
rows.anchor: وبفتح اللام كان مختارا للرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nidāʾ is raising one's voice to call someone.
rows.anchor: النداء: رفع الصوت بطريقة: يا فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyy is someone singled out to hear another's speech; the word relates to elevation and deliverance.
rows.anchor: النجي: المختص بإدراك كلام من يكلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyyan is a circumstantial expression: God honored Moses while speaking to him.
rows.anchor: نجيا نصب على الحال، أي: شرفناه في حال كلامنا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain's right side may mean its eastern side or the side to Moses' right; the Ṭūr is said to be in Syria.
rows.anchor: يعني كان النداء من جانب اليمين من الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drawing near may mean elevation in rank and being spoken to directly; other accounts place Moses near the Tablet or highest veils to hear the pen.
rows.anchor: قربناه في المنزلة، محله محل من قربه مولاه من مجلس كرامته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Reports say Moses was near the Preserved Tablet or the highest veils, hearing the pen's sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قرب من أعلى الحجب حتى سمع صرير القلم، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness cannot mean spatial proximity to God, who is exalted beyond place.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز حمله على قرب المكان من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Aaron as mercy and support for Moses, who had asked for his brother as minister and partner.
rows.anchor: لما أرسله دعا أن يشد ظهره به ويجعله وزيره وشريكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael is Abraham's eldest son by Hagar.
rows.anchor: هو أكبر ولد إبراهيم، وأمه هاجر

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm transmits another identification of Ishmael as the prophet who informed the Israelites about Saul; the author says consensus rejects it.
rows.anchor: أنه النبي الذي أخبرهم عن طالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣādiq al-waʿd means he did not break promises; messenger and prophet together can emphasize, add rank, or mean God sent him.
rows.anchor: إنه كان صادق الوعد أي: لا يخلف وعده

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Ishmael kept a promise to wait for a man, staying three days until he returned.
rows.anchor: وعد رجلا أن يقيم ولا يبرح حتى يرجع إليه فأقام ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another report says Ishmael waited a full year for the promised person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أقام حولا، عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: He may have been faithful to his promise to God rather than a person.
rows.anchor: كان صادق الوعد فيما بينه وبين ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukiyyan may be a verbal noun from the verb 'to weep.'
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا بكى يبكي بكاء وبكيا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use kasra on bāʾ in بكيا; the others use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: بكيا بكسر الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍamma on yāʾ in يدخلون makes it passive; fatḥa makes the people themselves the subject.
rows.anchor: يدخلون بضم الياء على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads الصلاة in the plural; the common reading is collective singular.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: الصلوات على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlī means great in elevation and capacity over affairs; it is also an attribute of God.
rows.anchor: العلي: العظيم العلو، والعلي: العظيم فيما يقدر على الأمور

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Bukiyyan is the plural of bākin, a weeper; it follows plural patterns such as khushūʿ and ḥuḍūr, and its original form was بكوي.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: بكي جمع باك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A short form refers to crying with tears, while the longer form has wailing and shouting.
rows.anchor: إذا دمعت العين فهو مقصور، فإذا كان ثم نشيج وصياح فهو ممدود

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Khalaf with fatḥa names a righteous successor and with sukūn a bad successor, though the forms may trade places.
rows.anchor: الخلف بفتح اللام في الصالح، وبسكونها في الخلف السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn means residence or staying in a place.
rows.anchor: والعدن: الإقامة، عدن بالمكان أقام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾtiyy is the passive participle from coming, with wāw and yāʾ assimilated.
rows.anchor: والمأتي: مفعول من الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujjadan is a circumstantial accusative; another parse treats it as specification.
rows.anchor: سجدا نصب على الحال، وقيل: على التفسير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The exception may attach to ghayy: those who believe will not meet it; al-Ḥasan treats it as an exception from the preceding clause and a new topic.
rows.anchor: من قوله: غيا، كأنه قيل: من آمن لا يلقون غيا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Alternatively it is a disconnected exception with an implied 'but those who repent.'
rows.anchor: بل استثناء منقطع بتقدير: لكن من تاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: It may instead be an exception from khalaf, the successors who squandered prayer.
rows.anchor: هو استثناء من الخلف، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word جنات is accusative with an implied verb: 'they enter gardens of Eden.'
rows.anchor: جنات في محل النصب بتقدير: يدخلون جنات عدن

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The clause about those God guided and chose may have been revealed about believing People of the Book, including ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām and his companions.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (وممن هدينا واجتبينا) في مؤمني أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes the passage as general.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Idris proposing to the Angel of Death, entering Hell and Paradise, and refusing to leave Paradise is padding and attributes impermissible requests and acts to prophets, angels, and God.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك حشو لا يجوز على الأنبياء والملائكة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: God's favor to the prophets means prophethood, or reward and other religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: قيل: بالنبوة، وقيل: بالثواب وسائر نعم الدين والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lineage divisions explain differing ranks of noble ancestry: Idris is Noah's grandfather; Abraham descends from Noah through Shem; the later prophets descend from Abraham or Israel through Mary.
rows.anchor: للبيان عن مراتبهم في شرف النسب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The phrase 'among those We guided and chose' may begin a new sentence about other nations selected by God.
rows.anchor: تم الكلام عند قوله: إسرائيل ثم ابتدأ الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it describes the named prophets as chosen for prophethood and guided to truth.
rows.anchor: بل المراد الأنبياء الذين تقدم ذكرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The signs of the Merciful may mean His religion.
rows.anchor: قيل: دينه، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: They may mean scriptures containing God's proofs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كتبه المضمنة بحجته، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They may mean the Qur'an; other views say warnings, every command or promise, or worldly punishments of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القرآن، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets prostrate and weep because God's signs make believers tender and tearful, even people of exalted rank.
rows.anchor: لأن آيات الله تورث المؤمنين الرقة والبكاء

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The bad successors may be Jews and their followers, since they descend from Israel.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم اليهود ومن تبعهم؛ لأنهم من ولد إسرائيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They may belong to this Muslim community; Mujāhid places them near the end of time after its righteous people are gone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم في هذه الأمة، عن مجاهد، وقتادة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Squandering prayer means abandoning it.
rows.anchor: قيل: تركوها، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وإبراهيم والقاسم بن مخيمرة وعمر بن عبد العزيز والضحاك
rows.claim: It may mean delaying prayer past its proper time.
rows.anchor: أخروها عن وقتها، عن ابن مسعود، وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Following desires may mean sins or permitting marriage to a paternal half-sister.
rows.anchor: قيل: المعاصي، وقيل: استحلوا نكاح الأخت من الأب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: It may mean permitting wine and other forbidden things.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استحلوا شرب الخمر وغيره، عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb satirically lists successors who drink coffee, play dice, follow lusts, neglect Friday prayers, and abandon prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن وهب: فخلف من بعدهم خلف شرابون للقهوات

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Ghayy may mean punishment, evil, failure, ruin, a valley in Hell, loss, or sins; Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Zayd cite a poem using it for failure.
rows.anchor: قيل: عذابا، وقيل: شرا وخيبة، عن ابن عباس، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of جثيا differ between ḍamma and kasra on the first letter.
rows.anchor: والخلاف في جثيا قد بيناه: بعضهم بضم الجيم وبعضهم بكسرها

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use a sākin zāʾ and light k in أولا يذكر, from dhakara, meaning 'know.'
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب: أولا يذكر الإنسان ساكنة الذال

rows.speaker: باقي القراء
rows.claim: The other readers double zāʾ and kāf, meaning 'remember and reflect,' from yataḏakkaru with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يذكر بفتح الذال والكاف مشددتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jithiyyan is the plural of a person kneeling on the knees; the original جثوي changed to avoid a heavy wāw-yāʾ sequence.
rows.anchor: الجثي: جمع جاث، والجاثي البارك على ركبتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shīʿa means a cooperating group or faction.
rows.anchor: والشيعة: الجماعة المتعاونون على أمر من الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣily means remaining attached and is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والصلي: مصدر، صلى يصلي صليا وهو اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtw means transgressing God's command and acting arrogantly; its original wāw was lightened to yāʾ, while another Qur'anic verse preserves the original form.
rows.anchor: أي: تعدى أمر الله واستكبر، والعتي أصل العتو

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as an indirect quotation: it is said, 'which is more defiant, let him come out.'
rows.anchor: على الحكاية بتقدير: فيقال أيهم أشد فليخرج

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Ayyuhum may be indeclinable in the sense 'the one most defiant,' after deleting an implied هو.
rows.anchor: أنه مبني، ومعناه الذي هو أشد على الرحمن عتيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author raises the question: how can the verse say the human was nothing if nonexistence is considered a thing?
rows.anchor: كيف قال: ولم يك شيئا وعندكم المعدوم شيء؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'He was nothing' means he was not something remembered or present, as in 76:1; the point is gratitude for bringing a living person into existence.
rows.anchor: أن المراد لم يكن شيئا مذكورا كقوله تعالى: (هل أتى على الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath tells Muhammad or any hearer that God will gather creation for resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: لنحشرنهم أي لنجمعنهم يعني يجمع الخلق في المعاد للجزاء

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The unbelievers may be chained to the devils who misled them for additional punishment; another view says they emerge chained to their devil allies.
rows.anchor: فيقرن كل شيطان بكافر منكر للبعث بسلسلة زيادة في عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is general rather than restricted to Quraysh's leaders.
rows.anchor: والأول الوجه لعموم اللفظ

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Jithiyyan means kneeling, showing helplessness, entreaty, and abasement.
rows.anchor: قيل: جاثية على الركب، عن الحسن، والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: It may mean groups or companies, like the plural of a heap.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جماعات جماعات، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: It may mean everyone gathered together.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جميعا، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands that the most defiant be selected from every faction.
rows.anchor: يأمر الله من ينزع من بينهممن كل شيعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: ʿAtiyyan can mean wickedness and lying.
rows.anchor: قيل: فجورا وكذبا، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: It can mean arrogance or superiority.
rows.anchor: وقيل: علوا، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: It can mean the leader and head of a faction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قائدهم ورأسهم في الشيء، عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: الأحوص ومجاهد
rows.claim: God may begin with the faction having the most adherents.
rows.anchor: نبدأ بالأكثر حزبا فالأكثر، عن الأحوص، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eternally knows who most deserves Hell; knowledge does not arise anew because He knows by His essence.
rows.anchor: لا يحدث لله علم؛ إذ هو عالم لذاته لم يزل ولا يزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment is God's right and He could forgo it; revelation establishes the gathering of all, while resurrection is intrinsically required for those owed reward or compensation not received in life.
rows.anchor: لأن العقاب حق لله تعالى، وكان له ألا يستوفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat about the most defiant shows that each is punished in proportion to their sin.
rows.anchor: (أشد على الرحمن عتيا) على أنه يعاقب كل أحد على قدر ذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatm can mean a decisive cutting off or a firm resolution.
rows.anchor: والحتم: القطع بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic idiom وردت بلدا means I entered a town; Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir are also said to report this use.
rows.anchor: ويقال: وردت بلد كذا كذا، والمراد: دخلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some understand warūd as entry, citing that God led Pharaoh's people into the Fire and that worshippers and idols enter Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الورود الدخول، واستدلوا بقوله تعالى: (فأوردهم النار)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir use warūd for entry; the word may be literal in both senses or literal in one and figurative in the other.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس، وجابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation of ḥatm is a firm resolution of the matter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إحكام الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadī is a gathering place, synonymous with nādī; Dār al-Nadwa in Mecca was Quraysh's council hall.
rows.anchor: والندي: المجلس الذي قد اجتمع فيه أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadawtu al-qawma means I gathered the people in an assembly.
rows.anchor: ندوت القوم أندوهم ندوا إذا جمعتهم في مجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line uses nadā for generous company.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: ودعيت في أولي الندى

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Athāth is household goods such as furniture and clothing; al-Aṣamm gives it a singular form.
rows.anchor: واحدها: أثاثة، كحمام وحمامة، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says athāth has no singular and gives alternative plural forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: لا واحد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾy is the visible outward condition seen in a group; the noun names what is seen.
rows.anchor: والرئي: ما يراه الرجل من ظاهر أحوال القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jithiyyan may be a verbal noun or a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: جثيا قيل: نصب على المصدر، وقيل: على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatman is the predicate of kāna, with the implied subject being arrival at the Fire.
rows.anchor: حتما مقضيا نصب؛ لأنه خبر (كان) تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadiyyan is an accusative of specification.
rows.anchor: نديا نصب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives 'torment or the Hour' may explain what was promised, be the object of seeing, or complete an implied clause.
rows.anchor: إما العذاب وإما الساعة قيل: نصب على التفسير

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The passage about unbelievers boasting was reportedly revealed concerning al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith and Quraysh challenging poor Muslims.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: وإذا تتلى عليهم ... الآية. في النضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grammatical ellipsis makes 'none of you except its arriver' mean 'none except one who arrives'; the Qur'anic and poetic constructions illustrate this.
rows.anchor: تقديره: ما منكم إلا من هو واردها

rows.speaker: عكرمة والأصم والقاضي
rows.claim: One view restricts arrival at Hell to polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد المشركين، عن عكرمة، والأصم، والقاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the threat as general and differs over whether arrival means entry or approach.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عام إلا واردها اختلفوا في هذا الورود

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An entry interpretation may address unbelievers alone, with 'then We save' beginning a new sentence, or all morally responsible people, with the Fire cool and safe for believers.
rows.anchor: فقيل: إنه خطاب للكفار خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal entry increases believers' joy, unbelievers' grief at seeing their escape, and warns people to take the threat seriously.
rows.anchor: زيادة سرور المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan rebuked a laughing man who knew he would arrive at Hell but did not know he would leave it; al-Ḥasan never laughed again.
rows.anchor: هل علمت أنك وارد النار؟ قال: نعم

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet saying every righteous and wicked person enters Hell, which becomes cool and safe for believers as it did for Abraham, then God saves the pious.
rows.anchor: وسئل جابر بن عبد الله عن الورود فأهوى بأصبعيه إلى أذنيه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Warūd may mean reaching or overlooking Hell without entry; they cite those whom God says are kept far from it.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن مسعود، والحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: حفصة
rows.claim: Ḥafṣa asks the Prophet whether his hope that Badr and Ḥudaybiyya veterans avoid Hell conflicts with the verse; he cites God's promise to save the pious.
rows.anchor: وعن حفصة أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: إني لأرجو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Warūd may mean passing over the Fire and seeing it; this sight magnifies believers' joy.
rows.anchor: قيل: المراد المرور بها فيرونها، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Everyone deserves the Fire because of sins; only piety saves the one who escapes.
rows.anchor: ما منكم من أحد إلا وهو على حالة يستحق أن يرد النار بمعاصيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Upon your Lord' expresses an obligation to give due reward and redress an oppressed person against an oppressor.
rows.anchor: كان واجبا على الله ذلك، يعني الجزاء لإيفاء الثواب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view says entry into the Fire is necessary because God promised it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ورود النار واجب للوعد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatman means fixed and certain, while maqdiyyan means decreed.
rows.anchor: حتما أي: واقعا كائنا لا محالة مقضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those saved may be people who avoided shirk or all major sins; those left kneeling may be polytheists or all wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: قيل: اتقوا الشرك، وقيل: الكبائر كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jithiyyan may mean kneeling on the knees or being gathered together.
rows.anchor: قيل: جاث على الركب، وقيل: جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers boasted of worldly status and judged the afterlife by present wealth; that is no proof of their final outcome.
rows.anchor: وإنما تفاخروا بالمال وزينة الدنيا ولم يتفكروا في العاقبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Athāth is worldly possessions and adornment; raʾyan may mean appearance.
rows.anchor: ورئيا قيل: هيئة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو علي
rows.claim: Raʾyan can mean fine-looking appearance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: منظرا حسنا، عن الأصم، وأبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As wealth could not save earlier generations from destruction, it cannot save these unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كما لم يغن عنهم مالهم عند إهلاكهم كذلك لا يغني عن هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may extend the life of those astray to give them a chance to repent and complete the proof.
rows.anchor: فإن عادة الله الإفضال عليهم بالإمهال إبلاغا للحجة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, God extends respite by leaving the wrongdoer to his own bad choices.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يمده بأن يخليه وسوء اختياره، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command form 'let him live long' is a threat; respite will not save one who fails to repent.
rows.anchor: فليمدد صيغته صيغة الأمر والمراد التهديد

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: The promised torment may mean worldly extermination.
rows.anchor: قيل: إما عذاب الاستئصال في الدنيا، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Other explanations identify it as punishment at despair, in the grave, or by the sword.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عذاب وقت الإياس، وقيل: عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour means Resurrection and Hell's punishment; then unbelievers will see whether they or believers have the worse place and weaker supporters.
rows.anchor: وإما الساعة يعني القيامة وعذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say arrival means approach, a view Abū ʿAlī prefers; Ibn Masʿūd is cited. Jābir, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others say entry.
rows.anchor: وأن الحسن وقتادة قالا: هو القرب منه، واختاره أبو علي

rows.speaker: عكرمة والقاضي
rows.claim: Some restrict the verse to polytheists; al-Qāḍī adopts that view.
rows.anchor: وأن بعضهم قال: هو خاص في المشركين، عن عكرمة، واختاره القاضي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view includes all people but says believers enter without suffering; Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for it.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال: هو خطاب للجميع غير أن المؤمن يدخلها من غير تألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees unbelievers enter Hell and remain punished forever; this is necessarily known from the Prophet's religion and Qur'an, so its denier is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة أن الكفار يدخلونها ولا محيص عنها بل يعذبون دائما

rows.speaker: المرجئة
rows.claim: On sinful Muslims, the Murjiʾa say punishment eventually ends and the sinner leaves Hell.
rows.anchor: وقالت المرجئة: ينقطع عقابه ويخرج

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some outside the Murjiʾa say no believer enters Hell, even after major sins.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يزعم أن كل من آمن لا يدخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement concerns only the sinful among the people of the qibla.
rows.anchor: وإنما الخلاف في فساق أهل القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'upon your Lord' means wisdom may make duties incumbent upon God, contrary to determinists.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: (على ربك) أنه يجوز أن يجب عليه أشياء من طريق الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation depends on piety, contrary to the Murjiʾa.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن النجاة تتعلق بالتقوى خلاف قول المرجئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth and leadership cannot benefit a person at the Resurrection, as destroyed nations show.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن المال والرئاسة في الدنيا لا يغني عنه شيئا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing punishment brings regret, but regret then cannot help, save, or find a helper.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن من عاين العذاب يندم فلا ينفعه الندامة

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use the ḍamma form of وولدا in four places in this surah and two elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وولدا) بضم الواو وسكون اللام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use the ḍamma form in Noah and the fatḥa form throughout the other Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب في سورة (نوح) بضم الواو

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers use fatḥa on both letters throughout the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر بفتح الواو واللام في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats walad and wuld as equivalent, supported by two poetic lines.
rows.anchor: أنهما بمعنى واحد كالعدم والعدم، والحزن والحزن

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A Qays dialect uses walad as a collective and wuld for one child.
rows.anchor: أن قيسا تجعل الولد جمعا، والولد واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walad derives from birth and offspring; lexical discussion contrasts a foreign-born, Arab-raised slave woman with one born in Muslim lands.
rows.anchor: الولد: ولد الرجل، وأصله من الولادة

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī defines a talīda as born abroad and raised in Arab lands, unlike a woman born in Islamic lands.
rows.anchor: قال [القتبي]: التليدة التي ولدت ببلاد العجم

rows.speaker: ابن شميل
rows.claim: Ibn Shumayl says talīd and mawlūd both mean people born in one's own household.
rows.anchor: قال ابن شميل: التليد والمولد واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed etymology links walad to secure upbringing; mawlid can also mean newly coined speech.
rows.anchor: والمولد كل كلام محدث لمن يكن في القديم فاستحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalaʿa ʿalayya means someone suddenly appeared; the root refers to what is seen or where an affair comes to.
rows.anchor: ويقال: طلع علي فلان: هجم علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying uses ṭilāʿ al-arḍ for all the gold the earth can contain.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث: لو أن طلاع الأرض ذهبا
